Purpose & agency

Make the distant personal.

Environmental destruction often feels distant until we recognize its consequences in places familiar to us. MineScars uses AI to bring that connection closer, turning photographs into educational illustrations and connecting them to documented mining impacts in the Amazon.

Step 01 upload_file

Upload

A user uploads a familiar landscape photograph — a local river, public park or hillside.

Step 02 developer_board

Analyze on LinuxONE

SegFormer-B2 performs CPU-based semantic segmentation, identifying visual classes such as water, ground and vegetation.

s390x native
Step 03 schema

Understand & prepare

Python calculates class proportions, builds the edit mask and applies YAML-based instructions for the visual transformation.

LinuxONE logic
Step 04 magic_button

Technical integrity & operational boundaries

Scene segmentation, proportion metrics and pipeline orchestration run on the IBM LinuxONE CPU (Linux s390x). Generative inpainting runs on an external cloud endpoint, which receives the prepared image and mask.

Ethical computing & research intent

Only upload images you have permission to use. Segmentation runs on IBM LinuxONE; the illustration step sends the prepared image and mask to Replicate (FLUX.1 Fill). This educational tool visualizes illustrative scenarios and does not replace environmental impact assessments.

What changed in this illustration?

          

          

            

              

                water_damageVegetation canopy stripping
                
              

              
Tree canopies and shrub layers are cleared to expose sub-surface mineral pockets, reflecting industrial clearing seen across illicit extraction zones.

            

            

              

                invert_colorsTurbid slurry conversion
                
              

              
Clear water becomes stagnant, sediment-loaded pools, like those left behind by gravimetric gold sorting.

            

            

              

                landslideHydraulic sluice trenches
                
              

              
Grass and soil are hollowed into exposed subsoil gullies and tailing heaps, as carved by high-pressure water cannons.

Madre de Dios River Basin, Peru

Mapped loss

                
139,169

                
Hectares of Amazon forest lost to gold mining in Peru

              

              

                
Official audit

                
MAAP #233

                
Satellite validation report (2025)

              

            

            
In the Madre de Dios region of Peru, alluvial gold extraction operates along fragile tributary basins. High-pressure pumps liquefy river banks, leaving mercury-tainted lagoons where primary rain forest once stood.

            

              
Scientific context note: This comparison is a thematic educational connection to help people grasp the scale of ecological disruption. It does not imply that your location is subject to mining.
